deep.reconstruction:
This page is the continuation of §3 ('Stetigkeit der geraden Linie') in the draft of what became Dedekind's 'Stetigkeit und irrationale Zahlen' (1872), §3. Nearly all the wording reappears in the printed text.

Argument, completing the sentence begun on the previous page:
(1) Lay off from the origin 0 a length incommensurable with the unit, e.g. the diagonal d of the unit square, so d^2 = 2. The endpoint corresponds to no rational number.
(2) The implicit justification (mine): if the endpoint corresponded to m/n, then 0α and the unit would have the common measure 1/n, so they would be commensurable. That is a contradiction. Equivalently, there are no integers m, n with n ≠ 0 and m^2 = 2 n^2.
(3) Conclusion: the line L is 'infinitely more complete in point-individuals' than the domain R of rationals is in number-individuals. The published version says 'reicher'. This is a qualitative claim, not a cardinality statement: Dedekind gives no bijection or counting argument here.
(4) Programme: to follow all phenomena of the line arithmetically, Q is insufficient. The 'instrument' R built by creating the rationals must be refined by creating new numbers, so that the number domain gains the same completeness. Dedekind inserts 'oder Stetigkeit' in the margin, giving 'Vollständigkeit oder Stetigkeit'. That insertion is the origin of the printed phrasing 'dieselbe Vollständigkeit oder, wie wir gleich sagen wollen, dieselbe Stetigkeit'.
(5) Methodological statement: the usual introduction of irrationals rests on extensive magnitudes, defining a number as the ratio from measuring one magnitude by another of the same kind. Instead, Dedekind demands that arithmetic develop 'aus sich selbst heraus'. The next page continues: irrationals must be defined through the rationals, and the question becomes wherein the continuity of the line consists.

There is no computation on the page beyond the implicit irrationality of sqrt(2).
errors: The claim that the line is 'unendlich viel vollständiger' is heuristic and unquantified. It is not an error, but it should not be read as a cardinality theorem; Dedekind's countability result for Q (1873 correspondence with Cantor) is later.
The irrationality of the endpoint is asserted via 'bekanntlich' (Plato) without proof. This is standard and correct.

results.what: The diagonal of the unit square is incommensurable with the side, so the line has points corresponding to no rational number
results.usually_credited_to: Pythagorean school / Hippasus (5th c. BC); Euclid X; Plato (Theaetetus)

results.what: Programme: extend Q by created numbers so that the number domain has the same completeness/continuity as the line, and develop arithmetic purely from itself rather than from measurement of magnitudes
results.modern_name: arithmetization of the real numbers / construction of R from Q (motivation for Dedekind cuts)
results.usually_credited_to: Dedekind (Stetigkeit und irrationale Zahlen, 1872; idea dated 24 Nov 1858), alongside Weierstrass, Cantor, Heine, Méray

deep.surprise_reason: This is a draft of the well-known §3 of 'Stetigkeit und irrationale Zahlen' (1872), almost verbatim. The only small points of interest are the textual variants: 'vollständiger' later became 'reicher', and the marginal 'oder Stetigkeit' shows how the term 'Stetigkeit' entered the text. These matter to editors, not as new mathematics.

checkable.asserts: The length of the diagonal of the unit square is irrational, so its endpoint corresponds to no rational point.
The only integer solution of m^2 = 2 n^2 is trivial, so no m/n with n != 0 has square 2 (the diagonal is incommensurable with the side).
The diagonal of the unit square has length sqrt(2) (Pythagoras).

transcription_corrections: The folio carries the page number '5.' at top right; it is missing from the machine transcription.
'oder Stetigkeit' is a marginal addition in the right margin, with an insertion mark after the underlined 'Vollständigkeit'. The transcription places it correctly but should mark it as marginal.

The struck-out material between 'verfeinern' and 'durch' is a whole cancelled line plus a cancelled word fragment before 'eine Schöpfung'. The struck line seems to begin with something like 'Welche Vollständigkeit...' but is largely illegible; '[-...-]' is acceptable.

Underlinings in the MS are not recorded: 'keiner rationalen Zahl'; 'Die Gerade ist daher unendlich viel vollständiger an Punkt-Individuen, als das Gebiet der rationalen Zahlen an Zahl-Individuen'; and 'Vollständigkeit'.
The final line 'Daß' correctly runs over to page 6 ('solche Anknüpfungen ...').
